recaps.headline: Nobody's Perfect, and the League's Second-Best Offense Is Ninth
recaps.lede: The last unbeaten record fell on Sunday. But the real story is a line in the standings that should probably be illegal: Doug has scored more points than every team in this league except one, and he is sitting ninth — outside the bracket, looking up at a team he has outscored by more than two hundred points.

games.blurb: Serge and Vlad ended it. Christian McCaffrey — their keeper, kept at forty-three dollars — went for 30.7 and the perfect record is gone. Eddie did plenty right: 27.34 from Trevor Lawrence, 25.4 from Jaxon Smith-Njigba, 23.0 from Chris Olave. It simply was not enough, and for the first time since Week 1 there is nobody in this league without a loss. He keeps the top seed at 5-1 on points, so the damage is cosmetic for now.
games.stat: Christian McCaffrey 30.7 · Matthew Stafford 16.88 · Chris Olave 23.0 (NiP)

games.blurb: Nassar moves to 4-2 and leads the league with 903.46 points, a pace that still projects past the all-time record. But look at the other side of this one, because it is the defining injustice of the season. Doug has scored 838.82 points — second-most in the entire league — and he is 2-4 and ninth. He has outscored David's Warren World All-Stars by 201 points. David is eighth and in the playoff bracket. Doug is ninth and out. Six weeks of posting enormous numbers against whoever happens to be peaking that week.
games.stat: Kenneth Walker 27.9 · Isaiah Likely 23.9 · Tre Tucker 26.7 (G+P)

games.blurb: One point and thirty-two hundredths. David wins the tightest game anyone has played this year, and that margin is precisely the difference between holding the final playoff seat and sitting outside it — he is eighth by virtue of this result and nothing else. He did it while starting Darren Waller, who scored zero. Rich drops to 2-4 and tenth, and the defending champions are now in genuine trouble.
games.stat: Puka Nacua 14.0 · Zay Flowers 12.7 · Jordan Love 20.24 (SoC)

games.blurb: Last week Will and Fish started Tyler Shough, their six-dollar keeper, and watched him score negative 0.16. This week he put up 26.96. Add 28.5 from Malik Nabers and they are 3-3 and sixth, very much alive. Peter falls to 2-4 and has now conceded 811.98 points — second-most in the league — which is a tough way to lose a season. Germie Bernard's 25.7 was the lone bright spot.
games.stat: Malik Nabers 28.5 · Tyler Shough 26.96 · Germie Bernard 25.7 (RmT)

games.blurb: Freeman and Manan had won three in a row and were sitting fourth. They posted 81.78 — their worst of the season by some distance — got a zero out of Juwan Johnson, and dropped back into the 3-3 scrum. Andrew keeps climbing: three wins in four weeks, up to seventh, and his tight end Kenyon Sadiq managed 2.2, which for Sadiq counts as a productive afternoon.
games.stat: James Cook 24.3 · Drake Maye 23.8 · Braelon Allen 23.1

games.blurb: Jesse moves to 5-1 and second, quietly assembling the least dramatic excellent season imaginable. Paul and Nick put up 80.86 — the lowest score of the week — and fall to 1-5. They have been outscored by 256.88 points on the year and have surrendered 854.62, the most in the league by a margin of forty-three. Three Tamiki Cups between them and the Biggest Loser Consequence is currently theirs to lose.
games.stat: Brock Purdy 17.36 · C.J. Stroud 19.84 · Jayden Daniels 21.0 (ME)

notes: Gibbs + Perplexity has the second-most points in the league and sits ninth. The team holding the final playoff seat has scored 201.42 fewer points.
Five teams are 3-3, filling seeds four through eight. Three teams are 2-4, filling nine through eleven.
TheNYFootballTeam leads the league at 903.46 points — a pace of roughly 2,108 over a full season, still clear of the all-time record of 2,046.18.
Mendes' Eyebrow has the fewest points for and the most points against, and the gap between those two columns is 256.88.
Kenyon Sadiq has now started three straight weeks for The Bushwackers, scoring 0.0, 0.3 and 2.2. Andrew has won two of those three.
recaps.closing: Eight weeks of regular season remain. Five teams sit at 3-3 scrapping over the last seats, and the second-highest-scoring team in the league has to climb over all of them to get in. The worst regular-season record hosts the draft party.

recaps.headline: Eddie Stands Alone, and Seven Teams Can't Separate
recaps.lede: The last two unbeaten teams met on Sunday and only one walked out clean. Behind them, the middle of this league has collapsed into a single undifferentiated mass: seven teams are 2-3, they occupy seeds five through eleven, and the Tamiki Cup cut line runs straight through the middle of them. Forty-nine points of tiebreaker is the whole difference between playing in January and hosting the draft party.

games.blurb: The only two perfect records in the league, head to head, and Eddie came out the other side at 5-0 — the last unbeaten team standing. He did it while starting a Bears defense that scored negative one point, which tells you how little the rest of the lineup needed the help. Jaxon Smith-Njigba, the keeper this team is named after, chipped in 22.8. Jesse takes his first loss of the season and stays second at 4-1 — nothing about this one looked like the start of a collapse.
games.stat: Trevor Lawrence 21.74 · Jaxon Smith-Njigba 22.8 · Matthew Golden 20.3

games.blurb: The 2023 champions opened this season 0-2 and have now won three straight, climbing to 3-2 and second in league scoring. Nobody is hotter. The loss, though, is the real story: Doug got 37.7 from Jahmyr Gibbs and 30.5 from Josh Allen — sixty-eight points from two players — and still lost by thirty-five, because Roman Wilson posted a zero and Harold Fannin managed 1.4. Gibbs + Perplexity now has the third-most points in the entire league and a losing record. The 2024 champion is scoring like a contender and losing like a cellar-dweller.
games.stat: Jaylen Warren 36.8 · Jared Goff 28.94 · Tyler Warren 21.4

games.blurb: Drake Maye — Andrew's K2 keeper at sixteen dollars — went for 39.46, the best individual score of the week. Bucky Irving added 31.5. Andrew has now won two of three after an 0-3 start and sits in the eighth and final playoff seed. His tight end Kenyon Sadiq scored 0.3, continuing a season-long campaign of near-total abstention, and it did not matter even slightly. The defending champion drops to 2-3 and ninth — the first team on the outside looking in.
games.stat: Drake Maye 39.46 · Bucky Irving 31.5 · James Cook 22.8

games.blurb: Track the $55 Puka Nacua across this season: a round 0.00 in Week 2 that became the league's favourite punchline, 27.7 in Week 4, and now 37.7. David has his second win and has dragged himself off the bottom. Meanwhile Serge and Vlad started the Raiders defense, which scored negative six points — not a typo, and the single worst starter outcome of the week in a week that featured three negative defenses.
games.stat: Puka Nacua 37.7 · Christian Watson 32.3 · Zay Flowers 18.26

games.blurb: Will and Fish started Tyler Shough, their six-dollar keeper, who scored negative 0.16 — and they won by fifteen anyway on the back of Malik Nabers and a vintage Jameis Winston afternoon. On the other side, Paul and Nick put up 126.46, which is a perfectly decent score, and lost. They are now 1-4 and alone in last place with the fewest points scored and the most points allowed in the league. Both ends of the ledger, same team, four straight losses. The man has three Tamiki Cups.
games.stat: Malik Nabers 29.1 · Jameis Winston 25.74 · Derrick Henry 21.0

games.blurb: Nassar's lowest output of the season and he still won by twenty-one, which says more about the opposition than about him. He leads the league in scoring at 761.18 and remains on pace for roughly 2,131 points over a full season — still clear of David Olesh's all-time record of 2,046.18. Peter was holding the final playoff seed a week ago and has now slid to eleventh, having been outscored by 134 points on the year. Still no Ridley on the roster.
games.stat: Isaiah Likely 32.4 · Joe Burrow 24.6 · Davante Adams 22.1

notes: Seven of twelve teams are 2-3, filling seeds five through eleven. The entire difference between the eighth seed and the ninth is 48.90 points of tiebreaker.
Three defenses scored negative points in the same week. The Raiders managed minus six.
Gibbs + Perplexity has the third-most points in the league and a 2-3 record. FreeManan has the second-most and is 3-2. Scoring is not currently correlated with winning in this league.
Mendes' Eyebrow has the fewest points for (516.88) and the most points against (737.62) — the only team at the bottom of both columns.
recaps.closing: Nine weeks of regular season remain. Eight of twelve make the Tamiki Cup, and seven teams are currently separated by nothing but points-for. One good week moves you four seats; one bad one costs you the same. The worst regular-season record hosts the draft party, and the league's winningest manager is currently holding that ticket.

recaps.headline: Two Undefeated, Six Tied, One Commissioner in Freefall
recaps.lede: Four weeks in and the league has split into three tidy groups: two teams who can't lose, six teams who can't separate, and four teams already doing math. The middle group is the problem — half the league is 2-2, and the Tamiki Cup cut line runs straight through the center of it.

games.blurb: Ninety-eight points. Nassar is now averaging 160 a week and leads the league in scoring by more than fifty points, and he is somehow only 2-2 — he keeps posting monster numbers against the teams having their good weeks too. On the other side, the winningest manager in Pegleg history is in last place. Three Tamiki Cups on the shelf, 1-3 on the field, and the most points allowed in the league.
games.stat: CeeDee Lamb 41.3 · Kenneth Walker 30.9 · Chuba Hubbard 25.9

games.blurb: The 2023 champions started 0-2 and have now won two straight by a combined 169 points. Nobody in this league is scoring more efficiently right now. Peter, meanwhile, is 2-2 and holding the eighth and final playoff seed by the thinnest of margins — he has been outscored by 113 points on the season and is somehow still in the bracket. Living entirely on schedule luck.
games.stat: Kyren Williams 36.7 · Nico Collins 30.8 · Bijan Robinson 27.7

games.blurb: Andrew gets his first win of the year, and he earned it the hard way — through three weeks he had been fed to whichever team happened to be hottest that week, absorbing the second-most points against in the league. Tetairoa McMillan went for 45.2, the highest individual score of the week. His tight end Kenyon Sadiq posted a zero, which at this point is less a disappointment than a tradition.
games.stat: Tetairoa McMillan 45.2 · Drake Maye 26.2 · Alvin Kamara 22.8 (JDC)

games.blurb: Jesse is 4-0 and has never once appeared on the Tamiki Cup honor roll going back to 2008. No signature star, no 190-point explosion — just four straight weeks of putting up somewhere between 120 and 145 and letting everyone else blow up and implode in turn. Will and Fish drop to 1-3 two years after their 2021 title.
games.stat: Ashton Jeanty 18.6 · Brock Purdy 19.6 · C.J. Stroud 21.5

games.blurb: Here is the best story in the league. Eddie owns the worst season in recorded Pegleg history — 3-11 back in 2022, the fewest wins anyone has ever managed. He is now 4-0 and in first place. Dave nearly caught him, and got a 27.7 redemption game from the $55 Puka Nacua who infamously posted a round zero in Week 2, but fell 4.56 short.
games.stat: Javonte Williams 31.3 · Chase Brown 19.1 · Lamar Jackson 18.9

games.blurb: Two-point-one-eight points. The defending champion opened 0-2 and has now won two in a row to climb back to .500, and did it in the ugliest possible fashion — 103 points, with a $49 Saquon Barkley contributing 2.0 for the second time this season. Doug was 2-0 and leading the league in scoring a fortnight ago; he is now 2-2, having lost this one because Ladd McConkey put up a zero.
games.stat: Tee Higgins 26.7 · Brock Bowers 20.6 · Ladd McConkey 0.0 (G+P)

notes: TheNYFootballTeam is averaging 160.5 points a week. Over a full 14-game regular season that projects to roughly 2,247 points — which would obliterate the all-time league record of 2,046.18 set by David Olesh in 2022.
Six of twelve teams are 2-2. The difference between the 3rd seed and missing the playoffs entirely is currently 201 points of tiebreaker.
Mendes' Eyebrow has the fewest points scored (390.42) and the most points allowed (595.54) in the league. Both ends of the ledger, same team.
recaps.closing: Ten weeks of regular season remain. Eight of twelve make the Tamiki Cup; the bottom four sail into the Will McKay Toilet Bowl, and the worst regular-season record hosts the draft party. Four teams are currently 1-3, and three of them have championship banners.

recaps.headline: The Champions' Reunion Happens at 0-2
recaps.lede: Two weeks in, the league sorted itself into four undefeated, four at .500, and four in trouble — and the trouble bracket was stacked with former winners.

games.blurb: The highest score anyone had posted all season, from the one manager whose name doesn't appear anywhere on the honor roll going back to 2008. He also quietly stopped starting his own defense against his own quarterback, which helped.
games.stat: Davante Adams 39.5 · CeeDee Lamb 35.3 · Dak Prescott 29.76

games.blurb: Doug got 69.8 points from two quarterback slots, which was roughly Dave's entire roster. Dave holds the all-time single-season scoring record (2,046.18 in 2022) and posted 75.8 with a $55 Puka Nacua contributing exactly zero.
games.stat: Josh Allen 40.82 · Patrick Mahomes 28.98

games.blurb: The 2023 champions scored a perfectly respectable 128 and lost anyway, which is the most infuriating way to start a season.
games.stat: Amon-Ra St. Brown 35.2 · Brock Purdy 28.48

games.blurb: Peter moved to 2-0 on depth rather than stars, and remained a man whose team is named 'Ridley me this' while rostering no Ridley whatsoever.
games.stat: Jonathan Taylor 29.2 · DeVonta Smith 27.7

games.blurb: Jaxon Smith-Njigba went for 42.5 — the best individual performance of the week — for the team literally named after him, kept at K2 for sixteen dollars. That is the entire point of a keeper league.
games.stat: Jaxon Smith-Njigba 42.5

games.blurb: The tightest game of the week and a loaded one historically: the league's winningest manager against the defending champion. Rich got 3.0 points from a $49 Saquon Barkley and fell to 0-2.
games.stat: De'Von Achane 12.3 · Garrett Wilson 16.7

recaps.closing: The 0-2 group was essentially a champions' reunion — the 2025 winner, the 2023 winners, and a two-time champ who owns the scoring record — while half the undefeated teams had never won anything.
